messages.subject: Replicate stratification -> error from dht2()
parts:
Hi everyone,

First, when trying to import an older Distance project into R with readdst, I keep getting :
Error in eval(parse(text = d_sel)) : object 'Label' not found

I would appreciate any cue on this, but in the meantime, I have set to actually redo the analysis with the distance package.

For context, this is a point transect survey repeated up to 6 times at 2 hours intervals, which was previously analyzed as replicates. So I wanted to first use ds() to get the detection function, and then use dht2() with a "replicate" stratification to get abundance estimates per survey "hour".

However, dht2() errors with :

Error in if (any(data$binned & data$distend > meta.data$width)) { :
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In data.frame(..., check.names = FALSE) : NAs introduced by coercion
2: In data.frame(..., check.names = FALSE) : NAs introduced by coercion

Surely, there's something I am doing wrong, but I can't figure this one out... I join the data and script. I would greatly appreciate if someone here had the time to look at this and give me a hint!

If it is any useful, if I put my hour variable into Region.Label in the flatfile, then I get proper (?) estimates. But then, if I understand correctly, repeats ("hour") are treated as "geographical" strata rather than as "replicate", aren't they?

Thanks in advance for any help.

Olivier

Olivier

I haven't gotten to the bottom of all your problems.  I would need your Distance for Windows project file (in .zip) form to be able to track down the problem with readdst​.

I also have not resolved the error dht2​ is throwing.  However, looking at your data, I'm not quite sure about the survey.  As you note, this is point transect data, but of an ungulate; I suspect you are located at vantage points.

For each of the 7 hourly surveys (and consequently also in aggregate), the greatest number of detections are in your most distant band (2900-3900m).  This band covers a large area (21km^2), so there are large numbers of khulan in the band to be detected.  But detectability does not seem to be dropping off as rapidly as the available number of animals is increasing.
When assessing the fit of the model to the data, the fit is poor (P = 0.019872 with 1 degree of freedom).

I was unclear also about the coding of the distances and the setting of cutpoints:  the data file contains:

> table(dat3$distance)

 200  650 1400 2400 3900
  24   18   57   71  102

while your setting of cutpoints for analysis do not match the values in the data:

ctpts <- c(200, 900, 1900, 2900, 3900)

Perhaps we could discuss further outside the email list, then you could report back to the list.
